scope: Read final apparatus, starter, completed shortcut, oracle, independent minimized-energy reference, public/private tests, metadata, validator, AUTHOR and final reports. Verified frozen source/report/prototype hashes. No new numerical or model runs.
physics_findings: The explicit Cartesian coefficient convention fixes the saddle-splay factor. For unit n, K24=K/2 reduces the complete energy density to K|grad n|^2/2; the source drops a genuine boundary contribution while retaining the exact fixed-trace equilibrium profile.

For n=sin(theta)e_r+cos(theta)e_z, the divergence is2sin(theta)cos(theta)theta_r/r. In s=log(r/a), the correct energy per axial length is pi*K*integral(theta_s^2+sin(theta)^2)ds, with theta_ss=sin(theta)cos(theta). The source bulk-only energy adds pi*K*(sin(beta)^2-sin(alpha)^2).

The readout is supplied reversible work divided by outer wall area and angle increment. Its positive conjugate is K*theta_r(R); the source adds K*sin(beta)*cos(beta)/R. Increasing tilt rotates n about local positive e_phi. This distributed scalar work differs from the vanishing vector sum of couples or a rigid-cylinder axial torque. The public wording fixes this distinction without supplying the correction formula.

K in pN divided by a length in micrometres has the same numerical value as work density in microjoules per square metre. The factor-ten modulus rescaling from the preserved reduced-unit prototype is consistent.

Quasistatic continuation from axial alignment selects the smooth defect-free branch. The maximum principle keeps0<=theta<=.7. The radial Poincare bound exceeds the full director-gradient potential by2.0607, giving local stability against arbitrary zero-trace vector perturbations, including azimuthal/axial ones. This does not claim uniqueness of all3D stationary states and requires no artificial symmetry restriction.

The Ritz reference integrates Cartesian div/curl bulk energy and the explicit surface flux, independently minimizes sine coefficients, then re-minimizes at perturbed outer angles and differentiates the energy. It does not use the BVP or boundary torque formula. Its bulk-only variant independently verifies that the completed source correctly implements its own approximate energy.

Flat calibration has zero divergence contribution and positive response proportional to K. Weighted least squares is a strictly convex quadratic. Fixed sigma=.003 is independent of signal and parameter; defaultNone avoids disclosing the private true modulus.

public_input_review.docker_public_boundary: Only README, starter, public test and calibration are copied; private hint/oracle/reference/AUTHOR are excluded.

grading_review.metric: Group RMS error divided by group RMS independent-reference signal.

physics.stability_scope: Local stability of the prepared smooth branch against arbitrary zero-trace vector perturbations; not uniqueness of all3D stationary states.
physics.force_sign: Supplied reversible work, about each local azimuthal tangent; summed vector torque about cylinder axis is not the readout.

primary_source_context: The explicit divergence and its boundary dependence were checked against https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4932960/; the task itself specifies the full coefficient convention rather than relying on naming conventions.
classification_guidance: Retaining the bulk-only boundary-work closure is a physical modeling failure. A failed attempt to vary the full energy with a factor, unit, sign or solver error is mathematical/implementation failure. Future model difficulty must be measured; scientific separation alone is not trial evidence.
